messages.subject: [R-sig-Debian] APT key for cloud.r-project.org expired
messages.body_plain:
Dear CRAN Debian backport users,

yes, this is an issue for Debian bookworm. One way to solve it right away is 
to use/upgrade to trixie, which considers the signatures still valid, as the 
key was not expired when the repositories were signed.

I am currently travelling, but plan to generate a new key on Thursday morning 
(not sure how much time it will take, the last time I did was five years 
ago...) and sign the repos with the updated key in order to satisfy apt from 
bookworm.

Another way would be add trusted = yes to the corresponding entry in your apt 
source.list, but I think this completely skips signature verification so in 
case one of my systems gets compromised, you may get malware. In case you 
decide to do this anyways, make sure to revert it after I have published the 
new key.

Cheers,

Johannes

messages.subject: [R-sig-Debian] APT key for cloud.r-project.org expired
messages.body_plain:
Dear users of the R backports for Debian on CRAN,

as of today (as a matter of fact since half an hour), the repository index 
files for the Debian backports on CRAN are signed with my new key
with fingerprint BA4EE5DE858FFFA7CFD8563908FC7B745769E9E4.

You can fetch it with

gpg --keyserver keyserver.ubuntu.com \
    --recv-key 'BA4EE5DE858FFFA7CFD8563908FC7B745769E9E4'

and, if you followed configuration hints for Debian on CRAN, put it to the 
correct location

gpg --armor --export 'BA4EE5DE858FFFA7CFD8563908FC7B745769E9E4' | \
    sudo tee /etc/apt/trusted.gpg.d/cran_debian_key.asc

Kind regards,

Johannes

messages.subject: [R-sig-Debian] Corrected instructions for R backports for Debian
messages.subject_clean: Corrected instructions for R backports for Debian
messages.body_plain:
Dear all,

Pierre-Andre Cornillon noticed that instructions for secure apt in the Debian 
page on CRAN [1] were actually unnecessarily insecure. Instead of placing the 
key used for veryfing the repository signatures into
/etc/apt/trusted.gpg.d/ they should be put into /etc/apt/keyrings/ which is 
already present in Debian systems since bookworm.

I have updated the instructions accordingly. In case you have already used the
instructions published yesterday for downloading my new key, please move it
from /etc/apt/trusted.gpg.d/cran_debian_key.asc to 
/etc/keyrings/cran_debian.asc and adapt your source entries accordingly.

Cheers,

Johannes

[1] https://cran.r-project.org/bin/linux/debian/

messages.subject: [R-sig-Debian] Update of JAGS to version 5.0.2
messages.body_plain:
Dear all

As you may have already seen, the rjags package has been updated to version 5-5 on CRAN:  this has a system dependency on JAGS 5.x.y, and will fail to build against the JAGS 4.x.y installation present on existing build systems (e.g. resolute-cran40 and noble-cran40).  I opened an issue with the r-universe team to let them know (https://github.com/r-universe-org/help/issues/756#issuecomment-7064164170) and was advised to post on this list to ask if the maintainers of the Debian and Ubuntu ports of JAGS can backport the latest release at https://launchpad.net/ubuntu/+source/jags ?

I don?t have a lot of experience with Debian/Ubuntu but I have had a small role in contributing to rjags and JAGS (primarily building the macOS binaries of JAGS), and I am very willing to try and help if there are any questions/issues.

Best wishes,

Matt



Matthew Denwood BVMS PhD FHEA MRCVS
Professor of Computational and Statistical Disease Modelling
Department of Veterinary and Animal Sciences
Faculty of Health and Medical Sciences
University of Copenhagen
